audio_unit.note: Identifies the installed plugin to scripts/audit_manifest.py, which re-derives every declared range and selector from it. Find another plugin's triple with `auval -a`.

description: Curated parameter facts for Neural DSP Morgan Amps Suite. Hand-maintained: this is the contract the generator writes against. It contains no Neural DSP code, audio, or preset content - only parameter names, units, and ranges needed to read and write presets for a licensed copy of the plugin.

/version.note: Plugin format version. Never write this - it is the file's own schema tag.

/selectedAmp.note: Chooses the live amp. All three amp modules exist in every preset, so any template can reach any amp. User-verified in the plugin.

pr12Amp/pr12Volume.note: PR12 is a 12W Princeton-style amp and it does break up, but THE KNOB POSITION IS NOT THE WHOLE STORY — how hard you hit it matters as much. Measured as harmonic distortion on a bin-centred 222.66 Hz sine at a modest input: 1.4% at 20%, 3.5% at 50%, 4.6% at 60%, then a knee between 65% and 70% where it nearly doubles (4.6% to 8.1%) and reaches 15% by 80%. Feed it three times as much signal and that knee moves a long way down the dial: 5% distortion arrives around 28% instead of around 66%. So quote a range, not a number, and remember `inputGain` and the guitar move it. Rendered offline — see docs/measuring-against-the-plugin.md.

pr12Amp/pr12Dwell.note: Spring-reverb decay. Morgan added it to the original Princeton circuit specifically so you can run a high reverb mix without washing the tone out — so for a wet-but-defined clean, raise pr12Reverb and keep dwell moderate.

sw50rAmp/sw50rVolume.note: Preamp gain, and the control that actually drives break-up: on a bin-centred 222.66 Hz sine it takes distortion from about 0.5% at 20% and 50% to 14% at 80% — flat and then a cliff, rather than a gradual climb. Note the output can exceed 0 dBFS up there, so trim `outputGain` rather than letting the next stage clip. Rendered offline — see docs/measuring-against-the-plugin.md.

sw50rAmp/sw50rLevel.note: Master volume: it is the loudness control and adds less dirt than `sw50rVolume`. Measured on a bin-centred 222.66 Hz sine, it produces about 0.3% distortion at 20% and 5.8% at 80%, against 14% for the preamp volume at the same setting. For loud and clean, keep this high and `sw50rVolume` low, but do not treat its top quarter as distortion-free. Rendered offline — see docs/measuring-against-the-plugin.md.

sw50rAmp/sw50rMid.note: MOSTLY A LEVEL CONTROL, not a mid band. Across its full travel it lifts the whole spectrum by about 7.5 dB, with only a further ~2 dB of emphasis around 1.6-2.5 kHz on top of that. (That pattern is what a passive tone stack with the mid pot in series would give, but the measurement is of output, after a nonlinearity, so treat the circuit explanation as a guess and the shape as the fact.) For comparison, `sw50rTreble` over the same travel is a real tilt: -3.4 dB at 59 Hz and +7.2 dB at 2.5 kHz. So reach for this to change how loud and how driven the amp is; reach for treble or the graphic EQ to change the voicing. Rendered offline — see docs/measuring-against-the-plugin.md.

sw50rAmp/sw50rBright.note: The real brightness switch, drawn as a sun/moon toggle. ON lifts the top: +1.3 dB at 1 kHz, +5 dB at 2.5 kHz, +8 dB at 6.3 kHz, still rising at the highest band measured, with the low end unchanged within measurement noise. Rendered offline through the plugin — see docs/measuring-against-the-plugin.md.

sw50rAmp/sw50rTrebleBoost.note: THE NAME IS MISLEADING IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND ONLY THE MEASUREMENT SETTLES IT. Writing this key moves the control the plugin publishes as `SW50R Bass Emphasis` — but turning it ON *removes* low end: -5.5 dB at 60 Hz, -3.3 dB at 100 Hz, and +2.5 dB from 400 Hz to 4 kHz, pivoting near 250 Hz. The same shape appears at two input levels 50x apart, so it is a filter and not a saturation artefact. In use it is BRIGHTER AND TIGHTER, not thicker. So the stored key name says treble and the plugin's own control name says bass; the sound matches NEITHER. What was measured is a low cut plus a 400 Hz-4 kHz lift, and nothing above 4 kHz was measured at all. Do not reason from either name. SW50R's dedicated brightness switch is the separate `sw50rBright`, which is a far stronger and higher-up lift (+8 dB at 6.3 kHz); use that for air, and this one to tighten the low end. Rendered offline through the plugin — see docs/measuring-against-the-plugin.md.

sw50rAmp/sw50rInputMode.note: Two input jacks, not a bright/normal toggle: `false` selects the control's `High` position and `true` selects `Low`. High is the default and the hotter input; Low is the padded input. Measured against the plugin — see docs/measuring-against-the-plugin.md.

ac20Amp/ac20Cut.note: HIGHER = BRIGHTER. Rendered through the plugin, raising this control from 0% to 100% adds treble monotonically: +5 dB at 1 kHz, +11 dB at 2.5 kHz, +15 dB at 4 kHz, and +19 dB at 6.3 kHz, with the low end within 1 dB. It behaves like a presence control, not like the Vox power-amp Cut suggested by its name. See docs/measuring-against-the-plugin.md.

ac20Amp/ac20BassTreble.note: A two-position voicing switch the plugin publishes as `AC20 Bass Cut`: `false` selects the `Bass` position and `true` selects `Treble`. ON is a large bass cut — -15.6 dB at 60 Hz, -10.9 dB at 100 Hz, and -8 dB at 160 Hz, tapering to -1 dB by 6.3 kHz — so it is brighter and much tighter; OFF is the fuller voicing. Rendered offline through the plugin — see docs/measuring-against-the-plugin.md.

ac20Amp/ac20Power.note: Not a selector: a continuous power control, stored 0.0–1.0 and shown as 0–100%. The example preset's `1` is 100%, not selector index 1.

pr12EQ/pr12EQHpf.note: The top of this range is 500 Hz. The plugin silently clamps larger values to 500.

pr12EQ/pr12EQLpf.note: The low end of this range is 1 kHz; the plugin silently clamps smaller values to 1000. At the top of the range the plugin displays `LPF : OFF`, so 20000 means the filter is bypassed rather than set to 20 kHz.

compressor/compressorRelease.note: Fast/slow release toggle: `true` is Fast, `false` is Slow. Measured against the plugin — see docs/measuring-against-the-plugin.md.

tremolo/tremoloRate.note: Used when tremoloSync is off. The plugin range is 0.15–15 Hz.

tremolo/tremoloSync.note: When on, tremoloSyncNote sets the rate and tremoloRate is ignored.

tremolo/tremoloSyncNote.note: Prefer `tremoloRate` in Hz with `tremoloSync` off. Note that this table is NOT the same as the delay's: tremolo starts at 1/32T, so every index is shifted by two against `enums.delayNote`. Used only when `tremoloSync` is on.

cabParameters/leftMicType.note: Index 10 is `Custom IR`, which is not a mic at all: it tells the cab to use `leftChosenIRFilePath` instead. Only set it together with a valid path — selected with no file, the plugin shows `Custom IR / No File`. Conversely, clearing the path without moving this selector off 10 leaves the preset in that same broken state, which is why --strip-irs resets both. Verified in the plugin UI and against the Audio Unit.

cabParameters/leftCabPosition.note: 0 = cap centre, 1 = cone edge, and cone edge really is darker — but it is a gentle tilt, not a tone control. End to end it is about +1.4 dB in the low mids against -1.1 dB at 6.3 kHz, roughly 2.5 dB of tilt in total — measured on the LEFT slot; the right was not measured separately and can hold a different mic. Use it to nudge; use a different mic to change the character. Rendered offline — see docs/measuring-against-the-plugin.md.

cabParameters/leftCabPan.note: Not a selector: a signed pan position. Negative is left, positive is right, 0 is centre; the plugin displays -25 as `25 L` and +25 as `25 R`. The ends are hard limits, so this cab cannot be panned past 50.

cabParameters/leftRoomMicType.note: NO CONTROL FOR THIS EXISTS IN THE PLUGIN UI. The cab page has two mics and a Room Send level; there is nowhere to choose a room mic type. The Audio Unit exposes it as a reserved slot named `R3`/`R6` with no value names, unlike every other parameter, which is the same story from the other side. It accepts 0, 1 and 2 and rewrites anything higher to 0. Leave it at whatever the template holds: a value written here cannot be seen, checked, or explained to the user. Verified in the UI and against the Audio Unit — see docs/measuring-against-the-plugin.md.

cabParameters/leftChosenIRFilePath.note: Absolute path to a third-party IR on the machine that saved the preset. Empty means 'use the internal mic', stored byte-identically to how an IR-free preset holds it. Clearing it is reversible, but it does change the sound. Use --strip-irs to make a preset portable.

delay/delayTime.note: Used when delaySync selects free-running mode.

delay/delaySync.note: You usually do not need it: leave it at whatever the template has and set `delayTime` in ms. `DAW` follows the host tempo and makes `delaySyncNote` the thing that sets the time; `Free` uses `delayTime`; `Tap` waits for the user to tap.

delay/delaySyncNote.note: PREFER `delayTime` IN MILLISECONDS INSTEAD: packs/timing.py converts a tempo and a division into exact ms (120 BPM + '1/8 dotted' = 375 ms), which needs no selector and leaves the delay free-running. Only use this selector when the user wants the delay to follow host tempo changes, which also needs `delaySync` on `DAW`.
